newsitem.title: USA: FSI sees year-over-year revenue fall.
newsitem.headline: FSI sees year-over-year revenue fall.

text.p: FSI International Inc, a producer of automated processing equipment used by semiconductor manufacturers, said it expects year-over-year revenue to decrease 8 to 12 percent in fiscal 1997 versus fiscal 1996.
"The semiconductor equipment industry is expecting a difficult year in 1997," said chairman Joel Elftmann in a statement.
Some analysts expect the overall semiconductor equipment industry to be down by as much as 10 to 20 percent, Elftmann said.

"At this time, we expect this slowdown to last until the second half of calendar year 1997," Elftmann continued. "We have put cost control measures in place to align spending with the expected sales decrease. Even though we enter fiscal 1997 with a good backlog, our visibility into the third and fourth quarter of 1997 is particularly low given current industry conditions."
Earlier, FSI posted August 31 full-year revenues of $304.0 million, up from $218.5 million.

For the full fiscal year, earnings rose to $28.5 million or $1.23 per share from $21.4 million or $1.13 per share. The current year results included a $1.5 million pretax charge for eliminating certain programs as the company implemented cost-control measures.
